vibe: Zimbra is under active fire, DeepSeek roars back with a $7.4B war chest and a plugin-everything coding harness, and OpenAI hits the brakes on its next model 'for safety.'

cyber.title: Critical Zimbra RCE flaw now actively exploited in attacks
cyber.summary: An unauthenticated SNMP flaw in Zimbra mail servers is being exploited in the wild for remote code execution. Corroborated by The Hacker News. If you run Zimbra anywhere, patch today — this is the day's clearest 'act now.'

cyber.title: CISA warns of hackers exploiting critical MLflow vulnerability
cyber.summary: CISA added an actively-exploited MLflow bug to its must-patch list. Relevant to anyone running ML pipelines or internal model registries — often left internet-facing by accident.

cyber.title: Critical Elementor Pro bug exposes WordPress sites to RCE attacks
cyber.summary: Unauthenticated attackers can upload PHP and run code on sites using the popular Elementor Pro page builder. Corroborated by The Hacker News. Millions of WordPress sites potentially affected.

cyber.title: ThreatsDay roundup: Gogs 10.0 RCE, n8n workflow-to-RCE, GLM-5.3 AI exploit, $10M reward
cyber.summary: The weekly grab-bag: a self-hosted Gogs Git RCE, an n8n automation-to-RCE chain, and a State Dept $10M bounty. Worth a scan if you self-host Git or run n8n automations.

cyber.title: AI-generated exploit scripts target Siemens S7 PLCs in US critical infrastructure
cyber.summary: Attackers are using AI-written scripts against industrial controllers — an early, real-world look at LLMs lowering the bar for OT/ICS attacks.

cyber.title: Citrix urges admins to patch new NetScaler flaws ASAP
cyber.summary: Fresh NetScaler/ADC vulnerabilities. NetScaler has a long history of being ransomware groups' front door, so admins shouldn't sit on this one.

cyber.title: isolated-vm flaw lets sandboxed JavaScript escape to host for RCE
cyber.summary: A sandbox-escape in a widely-used Node library for running untrusted JS. Matters to anyone whose product executes user-supplied code.

cyber.title: NASA AIT-GUI flaws could let unauthenticated attackers issue spacecraft commands
cyber.summary: Niche but eyebrow-raising: bugs in NASA's open-source ground software could let unauthenticated attackers send commands. More curiosity than to-do list, but a fun one.

ai.title: DeepSeek returns: $7.4B raised at a $50B+ valuation, plus a 'plugin-everything' coding harness
ai.summary: DeepSeek raised over 50B yuan (~$7.4B) at a $50B+ valuation in its first funding round, and shipped the fastest-starred GitHub repo in history — a new open coding harness where 'everything is a plugin' (model, tools, sandbox, even the loop), alongside V4 Pro. Corroborated by Fireship's teardown. The Chinese open-weight camp is very much back in the race.

ai.title: OpenAI confirms ChatGPT is down as logins and signups fail
ai.summary: A notable ChatGPT outage hit logins and signups. Now resolved, but a reminder of how much of the AI economy leans on a single provider's uptime.

ai.title: New context-injection attack could let web pages steal Grok chat data
ai.summary: Researchers show a cryptographic context-injection technique that could let a malicious web page siphon a user's Grok conversation. Part of the growing 'AI assistants as an attack surface' theme.

it.title: Bun 1.4 released
it.summary: The fast JavaScript runtime/toolkit ships 1.4. Relevant if you touch Node/JS tooling — Bun keeps chipping away at the npm/Node status quo.

videos.title: DeepSeek is back... and Silicon Valley is terrified
videos.verdict: SKIM — the news is all here in ~4 min; watch the middle only if you want the live coding-agent demo
videos.summary: Fireship's take on the day's biggest AI story: OpenAI paused its next-gen training run ('Astra') citing a cyber-capability threshold — which many read as cover for DeepSeek's comeback. DeepSeek's new harness treats everything (model, tools, sandbox, the agent loop) as a hot-swappable plugin — 'Linux for AI agents' — and he one-shots a working app for ~$30 on V4 Pro.

videos.title: AI Agents vs Business Rules: Which Should Make Decisions?
videos.verdict: SKIM — solid explainer, no news; the summary captures it
videos.summary: Clean breakdown of deterministic rules engines vs probabilistic AI agents, and why real systems use a hybrid: cheap rules handle the clear-cut cases, agents handle messy/unanticipated ones, with deterministic guardrails and a human-in-the-loop on high-stakes calls.
